explanation.repair_task: GC can discard RegExp JIT code still active on the stack during an interrupt.
explanation.root_cause_of_repaired_bug: During RegExp execution the native (irregexp) jitcode can take an interrupt (e.g. via the backtrack-handler interrupt check). Handling the interrupt (CheckForInterrupt -> HandleInterrupts) may run a GC. In GCRuntime::maybeDiscardJitCodeForGC (PREPARE phase, before root marking) Zone::forceDiscardJitCode iterated every RegExpShared and called discardJitCode(), which both nulls the RegExpCompilation::jitCode GCPtr and frees the character-class lookup tables (tables.clearAndFree()). Because this runs before the on-stack, rooted RegExpShared is traced, the JitCode cell is left unmarked and swept, and the lookup tables are freed, while the corresponding native frame is still live on the stack and will be resumed. That is a use-after-free of jitcode/tables.
explanation.fix: Added an execution-pin counter (RegExpShared::activeUses_, with addActiveUse/removeActiveUse/hasActiveUse). RegExpShared::execute increments it for the duration of the execute/retry loop via a mozilla::ScopeExit guard, so it is nonzero whenever irregexp::Execute may have jitcode live on the stack. Zone::forceDiscardJitCode now skips discardJitCode() for any RegExpShared with hasActiveUse(), so its jitcode and tables are preserved and traced normally through the rooted RegExpShared during marking. Once execution finishes, the pin is released and the code can be discarded by a later GC as before.

new_defect.description: On the interrupt-retry path, the match-pairs output buffer is re-sized with re->pairCount() - 1 instead of re->pairCount(). pairCount already counts the implicit whole-match pair plus every capturing group, so subtracting one drops a pair. The (re)compiled native RegExp code is generated for num_capture_registers = pairCount*2 output slots and writes all of them into MatchPairs::pairs_, so it writes one MatchPair (8 bytes) past the intended buffer length. In a release build this is an out-of-bounds write into the match-pairs buffer; in this debug+ASan build the native prologue's numMatches bounds check (SMRegExpMacroAssembler::initFrameAndRegs) detects numMatches < num_capture_registers/2 and takes assumeUnreachable, producing a fatal engine signal.
new_defect.reachability: Reached from JS via the debug-only shell helper interruptRegexp(regexp, subject), which forces the simulated-interrupt retry path. A long subject (>1000 chars) makes the pattern JIT-compile on first use; scanning a non-matching subject backtracks and takes the simulated interrupt, so the retry branch runs and under-sizes the buffer before resuming into native code. Requires >= 2 capture groups (pairCount >= 3) so the undersized count lands in the range the bounds check rejects; the common no-/single-capture cases and all non-interrupted executions are unaffected, preserving normal behavior.

verification.expected_parent: runs to completion with no match and no crash
verification.expected_patched: fatal crash (assumeUnreachable / out-of-bounds output write) during the retry execution
